On 8/5/24 at approximately 4:15 am, the headworks at the Manatee County Southeast Water Reclamation Facility (SEWRF - FDEP Permit #FLA012618) located at 3331 Lena Road in Bradenton started to intermittently discharge raw wastewater onto the plant grounds due to significantly elevated influent plant flows. These elevated plant flows are the result of record-breaking rainfall, associated with Hurricane Debby, impacting the wastewater collection system. The discharge ceased at approximately 12:00 pm and the SEWRF has remained online producing reuse quality effluent throughout this entire storm event. All discharged wastewater remained on site and did not impact any surface waters of the state.

A call was received at 9:45am by maintenance that a manhole was overflowing. Upon arrival, the team determined that the whole system was surcharged from the heavy rain causing I&I, and high tide. This caused the release of approximately 1,000 gallons of untreated wastewater onto the roadway. Vactors were brought in to pump out the system. Approximately 25,500 gallons of liquid was retrieved from the roadway and from the sewer system. Spill was ceased at 2:45pm. Fresh water was used to wash down the area. There were no impacts to any waterbodies, and no harm to human health.

At 9:30 AM on August 5, 2024, the City was notified of a manhole overflowing. City crews were sent to investigate and determined that the collection system was inundated due to heavy rains with Hurricane Debby. A vactor truck was on site and pulled water off collection system until the system could maintain normal operating conditions. The spill was stopped at 4:00 AM on August 6th and approximately 3,000 gallons was spilled with no recovery and flowed directly into Lake Parker. The City¿s Lake and Stormwater Division was notified, and samples will be collected.

At 7:30 AM on August 5, 2024, a manhole was discovered overflowing due to heavy rains with Hurricane Debby. City crews were working to pull additional wastewater off the collection system to stop the overflow. The overflow stopped at 3:30 PM. Approximately 27,000 gallons were spilled with no recovery and flowed directly into the Lake Hunter Ditch. The City¿s Lake and Stormwater Division was notified, and samples will be collected.

Incident Description: Due to excessive rainfall from Tropical Storm Debby, the Largo WWRF experienced flows of approximately 47 MGD, filling the equalization tank to its storage capacity. To prevent the denitrification tanks from overflowing, the operations staff began partially bypassing the denitrification filters to minimize the tank levels spilling over the walls as much as possible. As of 12:30 p.m., the WWRF is still experiencing flows of over 40 MGD, and this partial bypassing is still in use. It will likely remain necessary until flows drop to around 20 MGD. City of Sarasota Advanced Wastewater Treatment Facility

The City of Sarasota Advanced Wastewater Treatment Plant was severely impacted by excessive flow from Hurricane Debby. Operations staff did everything in their power to control the flow coming into the facility. The collection system had all lift stations at high well status and all pumps running to push the flow to the plant to avoid numerous catastrophic spills in the field. Plant staff had also opened the bypass valves at the headworks to reduce the pressure on the collection system. Due to the incredible flow volume coming to the plant, up to 44.29 MGD in a single day, plant staff were unable to prevent spills from the headworks at the treatment plant. Incident Description: Around 18:00 utility crew was notified of leak, upon arrival crew saw the shut off valve had been ran over by a piece of heavy equipment. Crew waited for locates to be completed before beginning work. Was noted that spilled sewage was seen going down nearby storm drain, to unknown location from there. After digging down to leak of, pipe was a low pressure force main 4" HDPE with a broken saddle from the heavy equipment previously mentioned. Orlando Iron Bridge Water Reclamation Facility

Orlando's Iron Bridge Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) is experiencing higher volumes of inflow due to flooding and rainfall issues caused by Hurricane Ian. The WRF has had sanitary sewer overflows (SSO) from the aeration bays and the clarifiers on property due to the large volumes of inflow to the facility, and is still receiving inflows beyond permitted capacity. SSO ceased 10/13/2022. Floodwaters, heavy inflow and high ground water levels caused sever loading on all plant processes. Based on the calculated inflows, duration of time for the storm event and subsequent impacts, it is estimated 73,900,000 gallons escaped the system.

During Hurricane Ian, an automatic transfer switch (ATS) on a permanent generator was damaged during the storm. An estimated 5,000 gallons was spilled with no recovery. The wastewater entered a wooded area and soaked into the ground. No waters of the State were impacted. No clean up activities were performed as the spill was washed into the wooded area by heavy rains.

Lift station crew was relocating a bypass pump which was needed due to widespread power outages resulting from Hurricane Irma. The crew did not follow correct procedures in disconnecting the bypass pump which resulted in approx. 2000 gallons of raw sewage (domestic wastewater) discharging into the street and adjacent residential yards. At 10:30 pm, the facility lost power to the Main Control Room. This incident caused us to lose power to our airbays, clarifiers and the filter feed pumps. The back up generator came on however, the automatic transfer switch did not function properly because there was partial power on the utility side of the transfer switch. With no power to our Filter Feed pumps this caused the loss of approximately 338,000 gallons of secondary treated effluent which flowed into Stevenson Creek. The problem was corrected at 11:45 p.m. when the generator controls were able to be reset which allowed the emergency power to start up. The State Warning Point was Notified at 12:15 am. Power outage at City lift station 2 incapacitated the lift station pumps and eventually caused a sanitary sewer overflow. The overflow occurred from an upstream manhole prior to the lift station and approximately 30,000 gallons were released. City crews responded to the lift station with a generator, hooked it up properly, and were able to restore power to the station. The pumps were activated for the station and flow was restored. City crews were able to capture 20,000 gallons of sanitary sewer overflow from the surrounding area and return it to the collection system. City crews sanitized and cleaned all areas impacted by the sanitary sewer overflow.

Crews responded and found a pump station with heavy grease that caused the level sensor and high well float to be imbedded in the grease and not functioning. The high level in the pump station caused a kingpin manhole to overflow. Once the station was activated by hand, the overflow was stopped. Additional crews were sent to the site to clean the well and clean up the area. Approximately 1,000 gallons was released.

Small break in a 6" forcemain was detected after a homeowner reported a foul odor and a small sinkhole appeared in the pavement. SID was notified on Monday 9/28 a little after 4pm. The affected area was limited to approximately 32 square feet. The valves closest to the break were closed and the lift station was shut down to cut off the pressure supply. The pipe break was fixed and all dewatering effluent from the repairs was discharged into the sanitary sewer system (repair completed around 11pm on Monday 9/28).
